results.text: Normal respiratory flora. No predominant pathogen isolated.

reports.text:
Indication: fever, productive cough, dyspnea.
Comparison: 09/09/2025.
Findings: New consolidation in the right lower lobe. The left lung and the right upper and middle lobes are clear. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Right upper quadrant surgical clips.
reports.conclusion: Right lower lobe consolidation, new since September 2025.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Seen 01/06/2026, arrival 19:15.

CC: cough and fever.

HPI: 63-year-old man, two days of fever with a cough bringing up sputum and breathlessness that has worsened each day. Past history includes Legionella pneumonia last July with an ICU course and a Candida bloodstream infection from his central line, both treated.

PMH: type 2 diabetes on insulin, CKD 3b, hypertension, hyperlipidemia; Legionnaires' disease and candidemia 2025, resolved. Lap cholecystectomy.
Meds: insulin glargine 24 u nightly, insulin lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: current smoker, 40 pack-years.
Family: father T2DM with nephropathy, died of MI at 68; mother HTN and CKD 3; older brother CAD.

Vitals: T 100 F, BP 120/80, HR 90, RR 20.

Exam: uncomfortable but speaking full sentences. Bronchial breath sounds with dullness to percussion over the right lower field. Heart regular. No edema.

Imaging: chest film shows right lower lobe consolidation.

MDM: community-acquired pneumonia of the right lower lobe. Given his recent ICU stay, line infection and diabetes, we want an organism if we can get one: sputum culture, blood cultures and urine Legionella antigen sent. Urine antigen negative. Ceftriaxone and azithromycin started.

Disposition: admitted to hospital medicine.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Received by fax 01/12/2026. Filed for PCP review.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 01/06/2026, discharged 01/09/2026.

Diagnosis: community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe.
Other: type 2 diabetes on insulin; CKD 3b; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; tobacco use; history of Legionnaires' disease and candidemia (07/2025).

Course: admitted from the ED with fever, productive cough and dyspnea and right lower lobe consolidation on chest film. Treated with IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin with steady improvement; afebrile from hospital day 2 and on room air throughout. Sputum culture: normal respiratory flora. Blood cultures: no growth to date. Urine Legionella antigen: negative. Home medications continued.

Discharge medications:
- Cefpodoxime 200 mg by mouth twice daily and azithromycin by mouth daily, to complete 7 days of antibiotics in total
- Insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime
- Insulin lispro per sliding scale with meals
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Amlodipine 5 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- Aspirin 81 mg daily

Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: primary care in 1-2 weeks. Smoking cessation advised.

PCP note on filing: reviewed. Will reach out to arrange follow-up.

documents.title: Back home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doc, you probably got the papers. Pneumonia again, right side, three nights in the hospital last week. Not the hotel kind this time they said. Finished the antibiotics Monday and feel mostly OK, just tired. Do you need to see me?

documents.title: RE: Back home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're home and feeling better. Yes, I'd like to see you in the next week or so: listen to your lungs, check your sugars and kidneys after the illness, and plan a follow-up x-ray in a couple of months. We can combine it with the diabetes visit that's due. Reply with a few times that work or text the front desk. If fever or breathing trouble comes back before then, call us right away.

documents.title: Blood pressure and cholesterol refills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy request for lisinopril 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg, 90-day supplies. Last seen 10/24/25; labs from that visit acceptable. Approved per PCP. Patient has not booked the follow-up offered in January; left voicemail asking him to schedule.

documents.title: Visits and screening due
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hello Mr. Alden, a reminder from your care team: you are due for a diabetes visit with labs, and your yearly lung screening CT is due this month. The CT needs an updated order from a visit. Reply here or text us with a few days that work and we'll find a time.

documents.title: Insulin refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting glargine and lispro pens plus pen needles and strips. No A1c since October. PCP approved a 30-day supply as a bridge and asked that he be scheduled before the next fill. Message sent to patient; no reply yet.
